title: Detonation Chamber: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Screening Console. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Screening Console
options.lineage: Checkpoint baggage X-ray consoles: false-colour material imaging
options.thesis: The artifact goes through the tunnel; its behaviour comes out as an X-ray, coloured by what it touched.
materials: translucent false-colour layers that multiply where they overlap
options.viewport: A single input line on top; beneath it a full-width scan strip that grows left to right as events arrive (orange = files, green = processes, blue = network, black = blocked), red boxes around contained attempts; ruled event log and verdict below.
options.risk: If the colour roles drift into decoration the strip turns into a pretty chart; every band must be one real event.

raised.raise: Panels tile edge to edge on hairline rules: no floating cards, no shadows, no whitespace padding.
One tabular monospace at data density for every number, timestamp and path; no decorative grey.
A band's length is its exact duration on the time axis; nothing is drawn longer for emphasis.
Selecting an event dims every other layer in the strip, so the selection reads at once.

regions.label: input: npm / pypi / repo / url + detonate

options.label: Process Monitor Trace
options.thesis: The tool analysts already live in: one dense, filterable row per syscall, with blocked rows highlighted.
options.viewport: Input on top, a full-height event table with columns time / class / operation / path / result, a verdict pane docked right.
options.risk: Also where most runs in this category land: instantly trusted, instantly forgettable on a demo stage.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: Airport departure boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: Every probe is a row on a live board; when something gets blocked the row changes state in place and stays lit until you've seen it.
materials: segmented pass with a scannable block
options.viewport: A live board of probes ranked by time; the verdict prints as a segmented pass with the IOCs as its scannable block.
options.case: Strong on clarity (held alert state is exactly the containment moment); weaker on audience identification: analysts don't think in flights.
options.risk: The pass metaphor can feel like a costume if the segments don't carry real fields.

options.label: High-Density Mosaic
options.thesis: Every signal packed into ruled modules on one screen.
options.viewport: A mosaic of ruled modules: files, network, processes, verdict, notes.
options.case: Density helps depth but buries the two-second verdict.
options.kept: Hairline-ruled panels with no whitespace inflation.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: The run as a strobing black-and-white barcode field.
options.viewport: A full-frame bar field with numeric margins.
options.case: Spectacular, but evidence becomes texture; analysts can't read it.
options.kept: Total commitment to a single tabular mono at data density.

options.label: Movement Score
options.thesis: Event classes as columns flanking a centre staff, time running upward.
options.viewport: A vertical score with files left, network right.
options.case: Elegant, but nobody in security reads a score.

options.label: Title Wall
options.viewport: Rows of past runs; focus expands one.
options.case: Browsing is not the job; triage is.
options.risk: Entertainment register for a forensic tool.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: The sandbox as a coloured map of zones.
options.viewport: A swelling lobe per zone: files, network, processes.
options.case: Playful register undercuts a forensic verdict.
options.kept: Flat unmodulated colour: no gradients, no glow.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The security-dashboard default: dark ground, KPI tiles, severity chips, a log panel.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, KPI tiles across the top, terminal and findings cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other security demo at the hackathon.
